Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of three line segments and an arc of a quarter-circle centered at $(-1,0)$ with radius $2.$ Find the value of ${\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$

${\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The graph consists of $3$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-3,-1]$, the arc of a quarter-circle for $x\in [-1,1]$, and the line segments for $x\in [1,3].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}.
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,-1].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since this region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{3}=-2.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}-{A}_{3} \\  & =2+\pi -2 \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[−3,−1]. The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

A1=12bh=12⋅2⋅2=2.

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[−1,1]. The corresponding region is a quarter-circle, so we find the area using the formula

The 3rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[1,3]. The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

A3=12bh=12⋅2⋅2=2.

Since this region lies below the x-axis, we have

∫13f(x)dx=−A3=−2.

Therefore, we obtain

∫−33f(x)dx=A1+A2−A3=2+π−2=π.
